sections.h2: Where is the Stark County Recorder, and what can I find there?
sections.html:
The Stark County Recorder is on the first floor of the County Office Building at 110 Central Plaza South, Suite 170, Canton, OH 44702. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It keeps the permanent record of deeds, mortgages and easements for all land in the county, and the office says those records are searchable on its website around the clock at no direct cost to users.

Stark County is the eighth most populous county in Ohio, with 374,853 residents counted in 2020. Canton is the county seat, and the other cities are Alliance, Canal Fulton, Louisville, Massillon and North Canton. The county covers 581 square miles in northeastern Ohio and was created in 1808. Because so many of the county's deeds involve older housing in cities such as Canton and Massillon, expect legal descriptions that run back through several owners.

Not every record sits here. The Recorder's page sends birth and death requests to the Stark County Health Department at 330-493-9904, marriage licenses to the Probate Court at 330-451-7755 and divorce records to the Family Court at 330-451-7415.

sections.h2: What does the Stark County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
The Recorder's fee page opens by saying the office does not set its prices: the Ohio Revised Code does, in section 317.32. The printed schedule lists $34 for a deed's first two pages and $8 for each more, with $4 for each cross reference. Since the statute lets counties add a preservation surcharge of up to $5, and another county on the 2025 schedule charges $39, phone the office before sending a check to confirm that $34 still applies.

The office accepts cash, check, money order and debit or credit cards, with a 2.75 percent convenience fee on cards. Make checks payable to the Stark County Recorder, and know that altered checks are refused. A published page-count chart on the fee page shows the combined total for documents up to 90 pages.

sections.h2: What must the Stark County Auditor stamp before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate transfer department, on the second floor of the same building, must endorse the deed first. The Auditor's page says a deed cannot be recorded until it carries the Auditor's stamp showing the conveyance form was filed correctly under Revised Code 319.202. The transfer line is 330-451-7333, with a second number at 330-451-7322.

  • The grantee files DTE Form 100 to declare value on a taxable sale, or DTE Form 100 (EX) to give the reason for an exemption.
  • A property that carries a homestead or the 2.5 percent owner-occupied reduction needs an additional statement of conveyance.
  • The conveyance fee is printed as $.004 on the purchase price, rounded up to the next $100, plus $.50 for each tax parcel.
  • The Auditor's office takes only a check or cash.

The Auditor recommends that an attorney prepare the deed, though it allows owners to draft their own. Both options still need the items below.

sections.h2: What belongs on a Stark County deed?
sections.html:
The Auditor lists specific content, and a deed missing any of it will be sent back:

  • The grantor's marital status, which supports the release of dower rights.
  • The grantee's name and the tax parcel numbers.
  • A current legal description that follows the county's conveyance standards.
  • A reference to the prior deed instrument. The tax map office no longer requires a stamped copy of the old deed, but the new document must cite it.
  • The signature of the grantor and of the grantor's spouse if married, whether or not the spouse is on the title.
  • A completed notary clause with the notary's signature.

Deed types the Auditor names include administrator's, commissioner's, executor's, fiduciary, limited and special warranty, quit claim, sheriff's, survivorship, trustee and general warranty deeds. A sheriff's deed needs a description approval form, and a probate transfer arrives as a certificate of transfer or a judgment entry. A transfer on death designation affidavit, unlike most affidavits, does not require a certified death certificate.

sections.h2: When does Stark County require a visit to the tax map office?
sections.html:
Any combination or split of a parcel has to go through the tax map office before the transfer. A split creates a new description, and the Auditor posts a New Legal Description Application, a Tax Combine and Un-Combine Request and a Condominium Requirements checklist for such cases. Sheriff's deeds need their own approval form.

In practice, a seller of part of a lot, a corner of a farm or a split duplex should call the Auditor's maps office at 330-451-7341 before a closing is scheduled, since a deed cannot be recorded until the transfer is stamped. Whole-parcel sales that copy the prior deed's description usually pass without this step.

sections.h2: Can I record or look up Stark County deeds online?
sections.html:
The Recorder says documents may be recorded electronically, with an E-Recording link on its website, and that the site lets anyone search the records free. Ohio law pushed this along: ORC 317.13 required every recorder to offer e-recording of conveyances and to put indexes and images online for instruments recorded since 1980 by June 30, 2026.

Copies cost nothing online. In the office, a self-serve copy is ten cents a page, and a staff-assisted copy is $2.00 a page. To get a certified copy by mail, send the Recorder a written request, the fee and a stamped self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: Which Stark County school districts and towns appear in deed searches?
sections.html:
Seventeen public school districts serve Stark County, according to Wikipedia: Alliance, Canton City, Canton Local, Fairless, Jackson, Lake, Louisville, Marlington, Massillon, Minerva, North Canton, Northwest, Osnaburg, Perry, Plain, Sandy Valley and Tuslaw. The district name often appears on tax bills and sales listings, so buyers who search deeds by address see it early.

Stark County also borders eight counties: Portage, Mahoning, Columbiana, Carroll, Tuscarawas, Holmes, Wayne and Summit. For land near a line, ask the Auditor's maps office which county's records govern the parcel.

faqs.q: What is the Stark County Recorder's address?
faqs.a: 110 Central Plaza South, Suite 170, Canton, OH 44702, on the first floor of the County Office Building. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: Is the Stark County recording fee really $34?
faqs.a: That is the amount on the county's published fee page for a deed's first two pages, with $8 for each added page. State law allows a surcharge of up to $5 per document, so ask the office to confirm the total before mailing.

faqs.q: Do I need the Auditor's stamp before recording in Stark County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Auditor's transfer page says the county recorder cannot record a deed until the Auditor has stamped it, which confirms the conveyance form was properly completed. Bring a check or cash for the conveyance fee.

faqs.q: Can the Stark County Recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts debit and credit cards, and it adds a 2.75 percent convenience fee on cards. It also accepts cash, checks and money orders.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a recorded deed in Stark County?
faqs.a: Ask in person or mail a written request, the fee and a stamped self-addressed envelope. The published price is $2.00 a page for staff-made copies plus $1.00 to certify each document.
